script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Workplace
Theme: forgiveness

Begin screenplay.

FADE IN:

EXT. MORNING - A bustling city park - 7:30 AM

A beautiful morning sun begins to rise as PEOPLE of all ages, races, and classes gather for their daily routines. Some jog, some walk their dogs, and others just sit and enjoy the day.

INT. COFFEE SHOP - 8:00 AM

Interior of a small but cozy coffee shop filled with the aroma of freshly brewed coffee. Customers engage in casual conversations as they wait for their orders.

At the counter, our PROTAGONIST, JAMES (30s, introspective, and kind), orders a cup of coffee. He scans the room and notices AMY (20s, ambitious, and sharp), a barista, serving a customer with a scowl on her face.

JAMES
(to Amy)
Another rough day, huh?

AMY
(sighs)
Just another one.

James exchanges a sympathetic glance with Amy and pays for his coffee.

INT. OFFICE - 9:00 AM

James works at a marketing firm as a copywriter. His desk is cluttered with papers and coffee cups, but there's a sense of calmness in his workspace. His colleague, RICHARD (40s, arrogant, and demanding), passes by, throwing a stack of papers onto James' desk.

RICHARD
(mockingly)
More of this garbage for you to clean up.

INT. COFFEE SHOP - 10:00 AM

James takes a break from work and returns to the coffee shop. Amy is serving a line of customers with a neutral expression.

James orders a second coffee and approaches Amy, handing her a ten-dollar bill.

JAMES
(smiling)
You've got this. Enjoy your day.

INT. OFFICE - 11:00 AM

James is back at his desk, working diligently on a new campaign. Richard enters and demands that James edit a proposal he's written.

RICHARD
(angrily)
Fix this garbage before I fire you.

James begins editing, focusing on the task at hand.

INT. COFFEE SHOP - 12:00 PM

James returns for lunch, finding Amy cleaning the espresso machine. He offers her a seat and they share a meal in silence.

AMY
(looking up)
Thanks for the kind words earlier. It means a lot.

JAMES
We all have rough days.

INT. OFFICE - 2:00 PM

James is wrapping up his workday, feeling exhausted. Richard enters, demanding to know why James hasn't completed a task he'd assigned.

RICHARD
(angrily)
What's the matter? Can't handle the pressure?

JAMES
(calmly)
I've completed everything you've asked of me. If there's an issue, let's discuss it.

INT. COFFEE SHOP - 3:00 PM

James returns to the coffee shop, finding Amy behind the counter, looking visibly upset. He approaches her, offering her a sympathetic ear.

AMY
(tearfully)
My mom was diagnosed with cancer. I don't know how I'll manage both work and taking care of her.

James listens intently, offering words of encouragement and support.

INT. OFFICE - 4:00 PM

James works late into the evening, determined to finish the campaign. Richard enters, impressed by James' dedication.

RICHARD
(surprised)
You've really outdone yourself this time.

JAMES
(smiling)
Teamwork makes the dream work.

INT. COFFEE SHOP - 5:00 PM

James visits the coffee shop one last time, finding Amy in a better mood. They share a moment of appreciation for their shared experiences.

AMY
(smiling)
You've made a difference, James.

JAMES
(gratefully)
And you, Amy, have reminded me of the importance of empathy and forgiveness.

They share a knowing smile as the sun sets, signaling the end of another day.

FADE OUT.
